title: Decide which tasks need attention

outcomes.can: Choose the correct branch at a threshold and distinguish equality from truthiness.

intro: A comparison such as count >= 3 produces true or false (a boolean). An if statement runs its first block when the condition is true. An else block runs otherwise. Braces group the lines in each block. === compares values for equality. && requires both tests to be true, and || requires at least one.

steps.title: Predict before running
steps.text: Read the example and predict what happens before checking your answer.

steps.title: Trace the example
steps.text: At exactly 3, >= includes the boundary and prints Busy. A number used directly as an if condition uses truthiness: 0 is false and other ordinary nonzero numbers are true. The empty string is false too. To ask whether a value is zero, compare it to zero explicitly.

steps.title: Check your explanation
steps.text: Read the indicated code and choose the explanation that accounts for its behavior.

steps.title: Include the last available place
steps.text: The supplied numbers requests and places are nonnegative. Set fits to true when every request can fit, including an exact fit. Fix the starter’s boundary mistake.

steps.title: Flag urgent work
steps.text: Use the contract in the exercise and check your answer on save.

questions.prompt: What prints for the example as written?

choices.feedback: The equal sign in >= includes three.

questions.prompt: If the condition were simply if (count), which count would select Room?

choices.feedback: Zero is false in this condition.
A negative nonzero number is also true.

review.evidence: Use a fresh answer on a later visit. An unaided pass on the changed case adds independent evidence. Preserve hint use and solution reveals with their attempts.
